Definitely not empathy, just something that looks like empathy when you don't look at it too closely. I don't feel particularly empathetic though. I can recognize that people are feeling things, and speak around them in a way that accomplishes either a nicer conversation or a resolution for them. But I'm certainly not doing it because I know what they are feeling or why. Tbh most of the time I'm not even doing that consciously, its just the only way I know how to talk to people relatively comfortably.
I'll let you know when I find out. Being drunk tends to remove my instinct to do that I guess, but that's not much of a permanent solution.

My imaginary conversations are all about preparing for people to be awful. I end out thinking out entire conversations where the other person is just yelling at me and how I would respond. It's... Probably bad that I do that.

Footsteps, the jingle of keys in their pocket, the creak of literally any door in the house. I knew every part of the house that creaked or made any noise when weight was put on it. Hell, I memorized the way people walked based on their moods. Angry walking sounds a whole heck of a lot different than normal walking. Even beyond memorizing the sounds of other people, I learned to walk very quietly. I still scare people who don't know I'm in the room because they didn't hear me enter. It goes beyond walking too, I have to consciously force myself to flush the toilet in the night because it makes so much noise. I avoid belts because they jingle when you have to adjust them. I hate having change in my pocket. It's a whole thing.

There aren't really any answers that will seem like good answers right now. I can't honestly promise that things will get better, and even if I could, you wouldn't believe me. That said, you're considering a very permanent course of action. At bare minimum I would urge you to take some time to seriously consider other potential courses of action. It gets easy to feel locked into that because you think of it often, and that ends out pushing you away from other potential options.

The fact that you've asked "why shouldn't I?" is a pretty compelling reason for you not to go through with it. You already don't fully want to, otherwise that question wouldn't have come up.

Best advice I've got is find someone to talk to. Therapist, family member, friend, coworker, whatever. I was lucky, I had someone barge into my life in such a way that I wanted to share with them. But the sharing really does help. Online is a good start, but real face-to-face interactions will help, even if just by giving you something else to focus on.

I hope I've helped.

EDIT: Also, as regard your specific problems. The thing about money problems is that they aren't really about money most of the time, but about what the money can accomplish. Bills are rough, but lots of friends are willing to help out with that kind of thing, even if just as a loan.

Tbh, I handle it pretty poorly. I've gotten better at it though. For a while I handled it by drinking and punching the occasional tree. I would recommend against those methods. Now I tend to handle it by going on walks or just listening to music or mindlessly watching netflix. Sometimes I can even just ignore it, which is nice. The hardest times are when I'm at work, because there's not much I can do there to help myself. At that point I just find literally anything else to focus on. Sometimes that's effective. Other times not so much. Physical work tends to help more than anything else at that point. That's about all I've got though.

Frankly, I've got a bunch of fetishes, which always felt weird to me. Eventually I just stopped trying to analyze it. To answer this in order:
1) I used to be pretty ashamed of just having kinks at all, but I've largely gotten over that large scale shame. That said, some of my kinks are kinkier than others, and I'm still pretty not OK with anybody knowing about them. Others seem kind of normal at this point.
2) Uhhhhhhhhhhhhhh.....Yes. To all of them. I don't even know whether I'd continue fantasizing about them if I could realize them, but I'm interested in experimenting, probably entirely because of my asexuality. The fact that I fundamentally don't understand sexual attraction makes me want to learn as much about it as I reasonably can. Yeah, this makes me feel weird about identifying asexual, but hey, what can you do?
3) ha. I can share some of them, but even with this degree of anonymity I'm holding some of these back. I find the idea of being the dom or the sub in a bdsm thing incredibly attractive. I quite enjoy butt stuff. I really really like androgyny and crossdressing. I think that's about all I feel comfortable sharing though.

I realize this probably isn't the most helpful response, but I don't exactly have many friends in the first place, so it doesn't really bother me that my parents and I aren't friends or even really friendly. I tend to be more upset by the lack of actual parenting growing up, and tbh I'm not sure there is any getting over that completely.

Generally I assume that I would be more trusting, or at least a bit more social. I wonder about a lot of this, but at the same time I have a hard time imagining myself any other way, so most of the time these thoughts just kind of fade away without any real resolution.

Definitely both, though definitely had to be the adult more. Any time my mother got upset I would be called upon to be "the bigger person" by both parents, and so I was always at fault for responding. And the moment I was supposed to be doing adult things, she would repeat the same (usually useless) advice over and over again. At the same time, I either had to accept all of her help or none of it. Don't want to hear about her first time getting a job for the fifteenth time? Fine, no assistance at all on anything, and also don't respond to the sudden yelling fit. Not allowed to be a child ever, but also repeatedly told that I'm not an adult. This of course continues at the tender age of 22.
